stem: According to Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
explanationCorrect: 'Let there be light' — God created light and separated it from darkness on the first day (Gen 1:3–5).

explanationsWrong.B: Man was created on the sixth day.
explanationsWrong.C: Dry land appeared on the third day.
explanationsWrong.D: The sun and moon were made on the fourth day.

stem: What was the sign of God's covenant with Noah?
explanationCorrect: God set the rainbow in the clouds as a sign that He would never again destroy the earth by flood (Gen 9:12–17).

explanationsWrong.A: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant with Abraham.
explanationsWrong.B: The Sabbath was a sign of the Sinai covenant.
explanationsWrong.C: The ark was the means of rescue, not the covenant sign.

stem: What was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham?
explanationCorrect: Circumcision of every male was the sign of the covenant between God and Abraham (Gen 17:10–11).

explanationsWrong.A: The rainbow was Noah's covenant sign.
explanationsWrong.B: The tablets belonged to the Sinai covenant with Moses.
explanationsWrong.D: Offerings were acts of worship, not the covenant sign.

stem: Who succeeded Moses as leader of the Israelites?
explanationCorrect: Joshua, son of Nun, was commissioned to lead Israel into Canaan after Moses (Deut 31; Josh 1).

explanationsWrong.A: Aaron was Moses' brother and priest; he died before Moses.
explanationsWrong.C: Caleb was faithful but not Moses' successor.
explanationsWrong.D: Samuel lived much later, in the period of the judges and kings.

stem: Deborah, the judge and prophetess, led Israel to victory together with
explanationCorrect: Deborah summoned Barak to fight Sisera, Jabin's commander (Judges 4–5).

stem: The sons of Eli who were condemned for their wickedness were
explanationCorrect: Eli failed to restrain Hophni and Phinehas, who treated the Lord's offering with contempt (1 Sam 2–4).

explanationsWrong.A: Joel and Abijah were Samuel's sons.
explanationsWrong.B: Nadab and Abihu were Aaron's sons.
explanationsWrong.C: Amnon and Absalom were David's sons.

stem: King Saul disobeyed God by

options.C: sparing Agag and the best of the Amalekites' animals

explanationCorrect: Saul spared King Agag and the best livestock instead of destroying everything as commanded (1 Sam 15).

explanationsWrong.D: David fought Goliath; Saul's sin was over the Amalekites.

topicName: A man after God’s own heart
stem: Which prophet rebuked David after his sin with Bathsheba?
explanationCorrect: Nathan told David the parable of the rich man and the poor man's lamb (2 Sam 12).

explanationsWrong.D: Gad advised David on other occasions, such as the census.

stem: King Ahab coveted the vineyard of
explanationCorrect: Jezebel had Naboth killed so Ahab could seize his vineyard (1 Kings 21).

explanationsWrong.B: Nabal was the foolish man who insulted David.
explanationsWrong.C: Obadiah was Ahab's steward who hid prophets.
explanationsWrong.D: Micaiah was a prophet who warned Ahab.

stem: Elijah demonstrated the supremacy of God over the prophets of Baal on Mount
explanationCorrect: On Mount Carmel, God answered Elijah by fire (1 Kings 18).

explanationsWrong.A: Sinai is where the law was given.

stem: King Josiah's religious reforms were sparked by the

options.C: discovery of the book of the law in the temple

explanationCorrect: Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law during temple repairs, leading to Josiah's reforms (2 Kings 22–23).

explanationsWrong.A: The return from exile came much later (Ezra, Nehemiah).
explanationsWrong.B: Jezebel was in the northern kingdom long before.
explanationsWrong.D: Amos prophesied in Israel, not in Josiah's reign.

stem: Which prophet is best known for preaching social justice, saying 'let justice roll down like waters'?
explanationCorrect: Amos condemned oppression of the poor (Amos 5:24).

explanationsWrong.D: Ezekiel prophesied to the exiles in Babylon.

stem: Isaiah saw his vision of the Lord in the year that
explanationCorrect: 'In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord…' (Isaiah 6:1).

explanationsWrong.B: Jerusalem fell over a century later.
explanationsWrong.C: Solomon lived about two centuries earlier.
explanationsWrong.D: Cyrus' decree came long after Isaiah's call.

topicName: The birth and early life of Jesus
stem: Where was Jesus born?
explanationCorrect: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:1; Luke 2:4–7).

explanationsWrong.B: Jesus was presented in the temple in Jerusalem, but not born there.
explanationsWrong.C: Capernaum was a base of his ministry.

stem: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before he was tempted?
explanationCorrect: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:2).

explanationsWrong.A: Seven days isn't the gospel account.
explanationsWrong.B: Twelve days isn't the gospel account.
explanationsWrong.D: Three days is linked with the resurrection.

stem: According to John's gospel, Jesus' first miracle was

options.B: turning water into wine at Cana

explanationCorrect: John 2:11 calls turning water into wine at the wedding in Cana the first of his signs.

explanationsWrong.A: The feeding came later in his ministry.
explanationsWrong.C: Raising Lazarus was the last major sign before his passion.
explanationsWrong.D: Healing the man born blind came later (John 9).

stem: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches mainly about
explanationCorrect: Jesus told it to answer 'Who is my neighbour?' — show mercy to anyone in need (Luke 10).

explanationsWrong.B: Forgiveness is the focus of the unforgiving servant parable.
explanationsWrong.C: Prayer is the focus of the persistent widow parable.
explanationsWrong.D: Growth of the kingdom is in the mustard seed parable.

stem: On the day of Pentecost, the disciples were

options.D: filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in other tongues

explanationCorrect: The Holy Spirit came upon them and they spoke in other languages (Acts 2:1–4).

explanationsWrong.A: Persecution and scattering came later, after Stephen's death.
explanationsWrong.B: Paul was taken to Rome much later.
explanationsWrong.C: The ban by the council came later (Acts 4).

stem: Saul (Paul) was converted on the road to
explanationCorrect: A light from heaven struck Saul down on the road to Damascus (Acts 9).

explanationsWrong.B: Antioch later became his missionary base.
explanationsWrong.D: Two disciples met the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus.

stem: According to Galatians 5, which of these is part of the fruit of the Spirit?
explanationCorrect: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control (Gal 5:22–23).
